text:
Deploy Bot: Canary deploy started for sdk-client v3.5 -> prod/us-west-2 (10% traffic). feature-flag=stream_chunking=true :rotating_light:
Alex Chen: seeing a spike in streaming disconnects and partial responses from mobile clients, + latency on paging endpoints :eyes:
Alex Chen: logs show repeated 'invalid_chunk_delimiter' and 'unexpected_eof' in the client framing layer
Alex Chen: example from logs:
```
2026-03-15T15:03:12Z ERROR stream-handler chunk: invalid_chunk_delimiter id=abcd1234 client=mobile-1
2026-03-15T15:03:12Z WARN conn conn_closed reason=unexpected_eof id=abcd1234
```
Alex Chen: errors start ~15:02 UTC, coincides with canary ramp to 10%
Morgan Li: I’m oncall and looking. Is this the new multipart chunking change from v3.5?
Alex Chen: yes, v3.5 flips on a new chunk delimiter semantics for streaming/paging clients to support resumable chunks
Jin Park: tagging eng-runtime and eng-ml. Potentially a client->server contract mismatch if older clients interpret delimiters differently
Sasha Rivera: I'm seeing similar in datadog dashboards — error-rate for /v1/stream up 18% in us-west-2 canary slice
Priya Nair: putting up incident banner on console and pausing new signups to affected routes. Setting severity=S2 for now
Oncall Bot: @Morgan Li assigned incident-2200456789. Runbook link: https://redwood/ops/runbooks/streaming-compat
Morgan Li: Temp mitigation plan: 1) hit kill-switch for feature-flag stream_chunking 2) rollback sdk-client canary to v3.4 if needed 3) notify CS and affected customers
Alex Chen: rolling feature-flag off now -> `ffctl set stream_chunking=false --env prod --region us-west-2`
Deploy Bot: Feature flag stream_chunking=false applied to prod/us-west-2 (propagated)
Alex Chen: flag removal reduced errors but some sessions remain in bad state (stuck partials). Will trigger a quick canary rollback next
Morgan Li: preparing rollback to sdk-client v3.4 for the canary group. Command: `redwood deploy rollback --service sdk-client --to v3.4 --region us-west-2 --canary-only`
Deploy Bot: Rollback started for sdk-client -> v3.4 (canary). ETA ~90s
Deploy Bot: Rollback completed for canary slice. Traffic should now be on v3.4 for canary.
Morgan Li: monitoring… error-rate dropping back toward baseline. Good signal.
Elena (customer): we saw failed videos for a handful of users during the window, ticket 7882 opened by CS
Customer Success: logged affected tenant ids, CS outreach in progress. No data exfiltration reported.
Jin Park: quick postmortem notes: root cause seems to be a subtle change in chunk delimiter escape sequence that older clients don't tolerate; server accepted the new format but produced frames that broke some client parsers. We introduced it behind a flag, but the canary exposed a broader client population (older SDK versions still used)
Sasha Rivera: impact estimate: ~6k streaming sessions touched in us-west-2 during 15:02-15:10 UTC, ~0.9% of total streaming volume, ~1200 failed requests, majority automatic reconnect succeeded but some user-visible failures (video/audio partials)
Morgan Li: mitigation done: feature-flag off; canary rollback; advise clients to upgrade to v3.5 when fixed. Next steps: 1) create hotfix branch to revert chunk delimiter behavior 2) validate against old-client matrix 3) staged canary with traffic gating and increased telemetry
Priya Nair: notifying PM and legal. Drafting customer message with CS: concise timeline + guidance to update SDK when hotfix is available
Alex Chen: quick repro added to the repo under /repro/stream-chunking with logs and harness. PR incoming (hotfix/stream-chunk-fix)
Oncall Bot: Handoff: Morgan Li -> Jin Park for remediation and postmortem. Morgan remains pager backup.
Morgan Li: assigning postmortem owners: Jin Park (tech lead) + Sasha Rivera (metrics/timeline) + Priya Nair (customer comms). Target: postmortem draft within 72 hours.
Alex Chen: note for postmortem: include matrix of client versions impacted and exact delimiter bytes; include test vectors to prevent regression
Priya Nair: CS update: initial outreach sent to top 10 affected tenants, templated notice queued for wider set; no SLA credits recommended at this time but keeping for review
Sasha Rivera: tagging follow-up: add regression test to CI, and run canary against recorded traffic from older clients before enabling feature-flag next time
Jin Park: will cut hotfix and run internal compatibility tests by EOD. Will not re-enable flag until compatibility suite passes
Morgan Li: closing canary incident thread — continuing remediation in engineering channel. If anything flares up ping me or page. :thumbsup:
